definitions.explanation: The hottest part of summer, roughly mid-July through August in Japan.

examples.japanese: {真夏|まなつ}の{太陽|たいよう}。
{真夏|まなつ}は{暑|あつ}くて{外|そと}に{出|で}たくない。
examples.english: In midsummer it's so hot I don't want to go outside.

examples.japanese: {真夏|まなつ}の{昼間|ひるま}は{気温|きおん}が{三十五度|さんじゅうごど}を{超|こ}えることもある。
examples.english: In the middle of summer, daytime temperatures can exceed 35 degrees.

notes:
Formed with the prefix {真|ま}- (true, exact), which here marks the peak of the season — compare {真冬|まふゆ} (midwinter) and {真夜中|まよなか} (the dead of night).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {真夏|まなつ}の{暑|あつ}さ: the midsummer heat
- {真夏|まなつ}{日|び}: a day with a high of 30°C or above

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {盛夏|せいか}: high summer — more formal and literary
- {晩夏|ばんか}: late summer
